**The meaning of the hadith**
Allah has made it easy for His servants to earn good deeds and the reward that will benefit them in the Hereafter: whoever helps a believer to do a good deed, the helper has a reward like that of the one who does it.

In this hadith the Prophet ﷺ tells us that whoever equips a fighter in the path of Allah, by preparing what he needs for his journey, whether from his own wealth or from the fighter's wealth, has fought, that is, he has a reward like the reward of fighting, even though he did not actually fight, without anything being taken from the fighter's reward. This is because the fighter can only go out to fight after he has been provided with this, so the one who helps the fighter is as if he were fighting alongside him. But the reward is multiplied for the one who equips him from his own wealth in a way that it is not for the one who only guides him or helps him without spending money.

Likewise, whoever looks after a fighter's family well while he is away in the path of Allah, and those he leaves behind, by taking his place in looking after his family's affairs and caring for them, has the reward of fighting. Whoever takes charge of the fighter's affairs and stands in his place in caring for his family while he is away shares in his reward, because he freed the fighter and spared him the concerns of his family and dependants; without this, he would not have been able to go out to fight.

The hadith urges cooperation in doing good.

📖 From the Hadith Encyclopedia — Dorar.net.

**Talk with your child**
1. Sanad was sad because he did not go out with the men. What were the two ways Mays showed him to have the reward of those who went out?
2. What did Sanad and Mays do for Layth before he left? And what did they do for his mother after he left? Which of the two deeds was "equipping," and which was "looking after his family"?
3. Why did Sanad's father not take his son with him, even though Sanad wanted to do good? (Because he was young, and the Prophet ﷺ used to send young boys back from fighting. So obeying his father was the right thing, and whoever has a sincere intention and helps as much as they can does not miss out on the reward.)

**This week's exercise**
Choose with your child someone who is busy with a good deed — a brother or sister getting ready for a test, a sick neighbour whose family is busy caring for them, or a relative who is travelling — and this week your child helps them with something they are able to do: preparing what they need, or doing a job at home in their place.
